title: Cap. IV Arg. 3: beneplacitum de salute = praedestinatio — 1 Cor. 1:21 Credentes velle salvare
latin: Arg. 3. Beneplacitum Dei de salute humana est ipsa praedestinatio ad salutem: Credentes velle salvare, est beneplacitum Dei de salute hominum: Ergo. Majorem dicunt esse perspicue veram, quia ipsa vox electionis nihil aliud significat, quam Dei beneplacitum de salute hominis electi. Minorem in ipsis verbis Apostoli fundatam ostendunt, 1 Cor. i. 21, Placuit Deo per stultam praedicationem servare credentes. Quod etiam a contrario illustrant, Quia Deus in hominibus minime credentibus non habet beneplacitum, sed anima ejus fastidit eos; juratque tales non ingressuros in requiem suam, 1 Cor. x. 5. Heb. iii. 18.
pass_a: Argument 3. The good pleasure of God concerning human salvation is predestination itself to salvation: To will to save believers is the good pleasure of God concerning the salvation of men: Therefore. They say the Major is clearly true, because the very word of election signifies nothing else than God's good pleasure concerning the salvation of the elect man. They show the Minor founded in the Apostle's own words, 1 Cor. 1:21, It pleased God by the foolish preaching to save believers. Which they also illustrate from the contrary, Because God in men least believing does not have good pleasure, but his soul loathes them; and he swears that such will not enter into his rest, 1 Cor. 10:5. Heb. 3:18.
pass_b: Arg. 3. God's good pleasure concerning human salvation is predestination itself to salvation; to will to save believers is that good pleasure concerning men's salvation; therefore. They call the Major clearly true, because election means nothing but God's good pleasure concerning the elect man's salvation. The Minor they found in 1 Cor. 1:21 — It pleased God by the foolish preaching to save believers — and illustrate from the contrary: in men who scarcely believe God has no good pleasure, but his soul loathes them, and he swears such will not enter his rest (1 Cor. 10:5; Heb. 3:18).

title: Cap. IV Arg. 3 Sol: same vice as Arg. 1 — Major terms incongruous; beneplacitum wider than praedestinatio
latin: Sol. Hoc argumentum idem fere est cum primo, et eodem vitio laborat. Sed iterum respondemus, In majore propositione terminos esse inconcinne et imperite dispositos. Nam Beneplacitum de salute humana est quiddam latius et generalius praedestinatione, debuit itaque praedicati, non subjecti locum occupare, hoc modo; Praedestinatio est Dei beneplacitum de salute humana: Credentes velle salvare est Dei beneplacitum de salute humana: Ergo credentes velle salvare est ipsa praedestinatio. Verum si hoc modo instituta fuisset major propositio, conclusissent ex omnibus affirmativis in secunda figura. Maluerunt itaque praeposteram enunciationem facere, quam manifestam παραλογισμόν committere.
pass_a: Solution. This argument is nearly the same as the first, and labors with the same vice. But again we answer, That in the major proposition the terms are incongruously and unskillfully disposed. For Good pleasure concerning human salvation is something wider and more general than predestination, and therefore ought to have occupied the place of the predicate, not of the subject, in this manner; Predestination is God's good pleasure concerning human salvation: To will to save believers is God's good pleasure concerning human salvation: Therefore to will to save believers is predestination itself. But if the major proposition had been instituted in this manner, they would have concluded from all affirmatives in the second figure. They preferred therefore to make a preposterous enunciation, rather than to commit an open fallacy.
pass_b: Sol. This argument is nearly the same as the first and has the same vice. Again: in the Major the terms are incongruously and unskillfully set. Good pleasure concerning human salvation is wider and more general than predestination, so it ought to be predicate not subject — thus: Predestination is God's good pleasure concerning human salvation; to will to save believers is that good pleasure; therefore to will to save believers is predestination itself. Had they framed the Major that way, they would have concluded from all affirmatives in the second figure. They preferred a preposterous wording to an open fallacy.

title: Cap. IV Arg. 3 Sol: if Major universal, false — declared beneplacita do not contain formal decree
latin: Sed permittamus eos suo modo agere: dico, nisi major propositio sit universalis, ex omnibus particularibus nihil sequetur. Si sit universalis hoc sensu, Quodlibet, vel omne, beneplacitum Dei de salute humana est ipsa praedestinatio ad salutem, tum erit manifeste falsa. Nam in quovis Dei beneplacito de salute humana declarato, non ilico exprimitur aut continetur formale decretum praedestinationis. Declaravit enim Deus in verbo beneplacitum voluntatis suae de qualitatibus et operationibus hominum ad salutem perducendorum, de mediis quibus eos uti oporteat, denique de toto ordine exsequendae praedestinationis: in hisce tamen non continetur electionis decretum, quia ex aequo ad omnes spectant, et per modum legis proponuntur.
pass_a: But let us permit them to act in their own manner: I say, unless the major proposition be universal, from all particulars nothing will follow. If it be universal in this sense, Any, or every, good pleasure of God concerning human salvation is predestination itself to salvation, then it will be manifestly false. For in any declared good pleasure of God concerning human salvation the formal decree of predestination is not straightway expressed or contained. For God has declared in the word the good pleasure of his will concerning the qualities and operations of men to be led to salvation, concerning the means which they ought to use, finally concerning the whole order of executing predestination: yet in these the decree of election is not contained, because they look equally to all, and are proposed after the manner of a law.
pass_b: Let them argue their way: unless the Major is universal, nothing follows from particulars. If universal — Any or every good pleasure of God concerning human salvation is predestination itself to salvation — it is manifestly false. In any declared good pleasure about human salvation the formal decree of predestination is not at once expressed or contained. God has declared in the word his will's good pleasure about the qualities and operations of those to be led to salvation, the means they ought to use, and the whole order of executing predestination — yet those do not contain the election decree, because they look equally to all and are set forth as law.

lemmas.gloss: proposed after the manner of a law

title: Cap. IV Arg. 3 Sol: beneplacitum that includes praedestinatio is the arcane will from the mass
latin: Beneplacitum ergo illud in quo ipsa praedestinatio includitur, est aeterna illa et arcana Dei voluntas, qua statuit apud se, ex eadem perditionis massa quasdam personas ex pura misericordia per gratiam efficacem ad gloriam infallibiliter perducere, aliis secundum justitiam in merita perditione relictis.
pass_a: That good pleasure therefore in which predestination itself is included is that eternal and secret will of God, by which he established with himself, from the same mass of perdition to lead certain persons infallibly to glory from pure mercy through efficacious grace, others according to justice being left in merited perdition.
pass_b: The good pleasure that actually includes predestination is not those declared statutes, but God's eternal secret will: from the same mass of perdition he resolved with himself to lead some persons infallibly to glory by pure mercy through efficacious grace, and according to justice to leave others in the perdition they merit.

lemmas.gloss: secret will from the mass of perdition

title: Cap. IV Arg. 3 Sol close: Minor true of medium — not eligere credentes; Rom. 9:15
latin: Jam accedo ad Minorem, quae illis Apostoli verbis constat, Credentes velle salvare per stultitiam praedicationis est beneplacitum Dei de salute humana. Quis negat? Est enim beneplacitum Dei de medio et organo, absque quorum ope ad salutem nemo adulta aetate perduci potest. Sed non exprimit illud aeternum εὐδοκίας beneplacitum secundum quod quidam ad salutem et salutis media, praeteritis aliis, eliguntur. Uno verbo; dixit Apostolus, Placuit Deo per stultitiam praedicationis servare credentes. Requirit igitur praedicationem, et fidem, tanquam media ex Dei beneplacito ad ipsam salutem efficiendam antecedanea. Non dixit, Placuit Deo per stultitiam praedicationis eligere credentes. Non igitur requirit fidem, aut praedicationem, tanquam conditiones praevisas et antecedaneas ad aeternum actum electionis. Neque huc faciunt quae de incredulis ex 1 Cor. x. et ex Hebr. iii. allata fuerunt. Ea enim loca non probant Deum ab aeterno eligere, aut praeterire homines ex antecedanea praevisione fidei aut incredulitatis in iis futurae; sed Deum in exsecutione aeterni sui decreti, tandem introducere eos in requiem suam, quos vocatione efficaci, et secundum propositum operante, reddidit fideles; eos autem excludere, qui proprii cordis corrupta perversitate manent increduli. Cur autem horum potius quam illorum misertus fuerit, noli quaerere, si non vis errare. Sufficiat illud, Miserebor cujus misertus fuero, et commiserabor quem commiseratus fuero, Rom. ix. 15.
pass_a: Now I come to the Minor, which consists in those words of the Apostle, To will to save believers by the foolishness of preaching is God's good pleasure concerning human salvation. Who denies it? For it is God's good pleasure concerning the means and organ, without whose help no one of adult age can be led to salvation. But it does not express that eternal good pleasure of εὐδοκία according to which certain ones are elected to salvation and the means of salvation, others being passed by. In a word; the Apostle said, It pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save believers. He therefore requires preaching, and faith, as means antecedent from God's good pleasure to effecting salvation itself. He did not say, It pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to elect believers. He therefore does not require faith, or preaching, as conditions foreseen and antecedent to the eternal act of election. Nor do those things avail hither which were brought concerning unbelievers from 1 Cor. 10 and from Heb. 3. For those places do not prove that God from eternity elects, or passes by men from antecedent foresight of faith or unbelief future in them; but that God in the execution of his eternal decree finally introduces into his rest those whom by efficacious vocation, and working according to purpose, he has rendered faithful; but excludes those who by the corrupt perversity of their own heart remain unbelieving. But why he will have had mercy on these rather than those, do not seek, if you do not will to err. Let that suffice, I will have mercy on whom I will have had mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have had compassion, Rom. 9:15.
pass_b: Now the Minor: to will to save believers by the foolishness of preaching is God's good pleasure concerning human salvation. Who denies it? It is good pleasure about the means and organ without which no adult can be led to salvation. It does not express that eternal εὐδοκία by which some are elected to salvation and its means, others passed by. In a word: the Apostle said It pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save believers — so he requires preaching and faith as means antecedent by God's good pleasure to effecting salvation. He did not say to elect believers. So he does not require faith or preaching as foreseen antecedent conditions of the eternal act of election. Nor do 1 Cor. 10 and Heb. 3 on unbelievers help: they do not prove eternal election or passing-by from foresight of future faith or unbelief, but that in executing his eternal decree God finally brings into his rest those whom efficacious vocation working according to purpose has made faithful, and excludes those who remain unbelieving by their own heart's corrupt perversity. Why he had mercy on these rather than those — do not ask, if you would not err. Suffice Rom. 9:15: I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy.

lemmas.gloss: I will have mercy on whom I will
